A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the childhood antecedents for adult psychopathology are weak for emotional disorders, moderate for schizophrenia and strongest for personality disturbance.
there is a strong continuity of behaviour disturbance between childhood and adult psychiatric disorder but the specific nature of this continuity is different for different conditions.
the childhood antecedents are most clearly defined for the conditions that have the strongest genetic components and least well defined for conditions with the weakest genetic components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the child-adult link is not a simple one and is not a simple function of the degree of similarity between the two disorders.
the most important childhood antecedents for adult psychopathology are not necessarily the ones most closely related in content to the adult disorder.
the childhood antecedents are not specific to any one adult disorder but rather are part of a spectrum of disorders.
